name: Autograph
funding: Arts Council England and the National Lottery Heritage Fund (site footer). Projects backed by Art Fund, Paul Hamlyn Foundation and Cockayne Grants. Barclays gave to the 2007 building only.
watch: Rivington Place opened in 2007 with Arts Council lottery capital, Barclays, Hackney, the London Development Agency and the EU. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: One yearly impact summary (2025 to 2026), accounts on the Charity Commission register, funder logos only, and trustees listed on the team page.

name: AZ Museum (Anatoly Zverev Museum)
watch: Opened 2015; half the collection donated by Aliki Costakis. OpenSanctions shows Opaleva only as a Russian company-register record, not sanctioned.
records_note: This private museum's site has no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; press says its founder funds it from her own money.

name: Azkuna Zentroa (Alhóndiga Bilbao)
watch: Former municipal wine warehouse converted by Philippe Starck into a public cultural centre. Wholly public.

name: B7L9 Art Centre (Kamel Lazaar Foundation)
funding: Opened 2019, funded by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation (money from Swicorp, a banking firm); partners include the EU, the German Foreign Office, Goethe, Pro Helvetia, Tunisair and Porticus.
watch: Tunisia's first non-profit contemporary art centre, in the Bhar Lazreg suburb; replaces B'chira Art Center, which has no recent record.

name: B7L9 Art Centre
funding: Run by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation, set up in 2005 by Swicorp founder Kamel Lazaar, a Riyadh-based investment banker; B7L9 opened in 2019 as its first permanent venue. The foundation's undated partners page names the German Federal Foreign Office, the EU delegation, Goethe-Institut, Pro Helvetia, Institut Français, Tunisair and the Tunisian Education Ministry.
watch: Swicorp is a Riyadh-based investment bank, not a state body. Lazaar once sat on the board of Creative Energy Resources, a power-sector holding. No controversy found for the foundation or Lazaar.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; the parent Kamel Lazaar Foundation names 18 partners and funders on an undated page and its founders and staff, but no board.

name: Baku Museum of Modern Art
funding: Opened 20 Mar 2009 with about 800 works; founded by First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva and funded by the Heydar Aliyev Foundation, which she heads.
watch: A ruling-family foundation is its only known funder; the director since 2012 is Aida Mahmudova, founder of YARAT.
records_note: The museum's site, live copy down, shows no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it carries only about, visit, library and what's-on pages.

name: Ballroom Marfa
funding: No donor list is published; the site credits 'individuals and foundations' without names. The FY2023 filing shows $589K in contributions on $818K revenue and $1.13M expenses.
watch: Free admission. Its guidelines bar fossil-extraction or defense underwriting, despite the local oil economy.
records_note: Its People page names 22 trustees, ProPublica holds Form 990s for 2004 to 2023, and a 20th Anniversary Fund donor page names about 38 givers.

name: Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM)
funding: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs, corporate sponsorships, box office, private philanthropy.

name: BAMPFA
funding: UC Berkeley unit; top supporters (2026 list) are Mellon, Hewlett, Luce, Terra, Warhol, IMLS and NEH; U.S. Bank Foundation and Google among firms.
watch: Hollywood Foreign Press Association is on the supporters list. A student labour demo at the 2016 opening targeted UC contractors, not a funder.
records_note: A UC Berkeley unit with no reports of its own; the University of California posts financial reports 2015 to 2025, BAMPFA names funders undated.

name: Bandjoun Station
funding: Small artist-run centre opened 2013, paid for by Barthélémy Toguo, his coffee plantations and the Amis de Bandjoun Station association.
watch: Residencies, museum and farm in the Bamileke highlands; MO.CO Montpellier sends graduates for residencies (since 2023).
records_note: The live site is down; its January 2025 archived copy has no reports, accounts, funder list or board, only project text and press.

name: Barbican Centre
funding: City of London Corporation funding, box office revenue, venue hire, commercial leases.

name: Basic Space
funding: The Arts Council of Ireland, Dublin City Arts Office, project support; nomadic artist-led collective.
watch: Nomadic artist-run organization challenging institutional hierarchies through decentralized, non-commercial projects since 2010.
